### Use useQuery with <script setup>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/installation.md

All documentation examples use the <script setup> syntax. Vue 2 users can use it via the unplugin-vue2-script-setup plugin; otherwise translate to normal Composition API by moving code into setup() and returning template values.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const { isPending, isFetching, isError, data, error } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: getTodos,
})
</script>

<template>...</template>
```

### build method example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/classes/QueryCache.md

Example usage of the build method to get or create a query for the 'posts' key.

```ts
const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()

const query = queryCache.build(queryClient, {
  queryKey: ['posts'],
  queryFn: fetchPosts,
})
```

### Call useQueryClient in a Vue script setup block

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Call useQueryClient inside setup() to get the installed QueryClient, then use it to invalidate queries. Throws if called outside an injection context or if no QueryClient was installed via VueQueryPlugin.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```

### Create withSetup helper for Vue 3 with VueQueryPlugin

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/guides/testing.md

Mounts a component, runs the composable in its `setup`, and installs `VueQueryPlugin` with a `QueryClient`. Returns the composable result and the wrapper.

```ts
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { flushPromises, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

function withSetup<T>(composable: () => T, queryClient = new QueryClient()) {
  let result!: T
  const wrapper = mount(
    defineComponent({
      setup() {
        result = composable()
        return () => null
      },
    }),
    { global: { plugins: [[VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient }]] } },
  )
  return [result, wrapper] as const
}
```

### Pass signals directly to useQuery arguments in Solid Query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Signals and store values can be passed directly into function arguments, and Solid Query updates the query store automatically when the signal value changes. The example uses enabled() and todo() inside the useQuery options function.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { createSignal, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const [enabled, setEnabled] = createSignal(false)
  const [todo, setTodo] = createSignal(0)

  // ✅ passing a signal directly is safe and observers update
  // automatically when the value of a signal changes
  const todosQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
    enabled: enabled(),
  }))

  const todoDetailsQuery = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todo', todo()],
    queryFn: fetchTodo,
    enabled: todo() > 0,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isError}>
          <p>Error: {todosQuery.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={todosQuery.isSuccess}>
          <For each={todosQuery.data}>
            {(todo) => (
              <button onClick={() => setTodo(todo.id)}>{todo.title}</button>
            )}
          </For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
      <button onClick={() => setEnabled(!enabled())}>Toggle enabled</button>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider and useQuery in SolidJS

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Create a QueryClient and wrap the app in QueryClientProvider, then fetch todos with useQuery and render pending, error, and success states using Solid's Switch/Match/For.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/solid-query'
import { Switch, Match, For } from 'solid-js'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function Example() {
  const query = useQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodos,
  }))

  return (
    <div>
      <Switch>
        <Match when={query.isPending}>
          <p>Loading...</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isError}>
          <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
        </Match>
        <Match when={query.isSuccess}>
          <For each={query.data}>{(todo) => <p>{todo.title}</p>}</For>
        </Match>
      </Switch>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### createQuery Example Checking isPending/isError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/functions/createQuery.md

Same query as the status example, but branching on the derived booleans query.isPending and query.isError instead of query.status.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['posts'],
    queryFn: fetchPosts,
  }))
</script>

{#if query.isPending}
  Loading...
{:else if query.isError}
  <span>Error: {query.error.message}</span>
{:else}
  <ul>
    {#each query.data as post (post.id)}
      <li>{post.title}</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{/if}
```

--------------------------------

### Run Lit examples on custom ports via environment variables

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/packages/lit-query/README.md

Optionally override default ports using DEMO_PORT, PAGINATION_DEMO_PORT, PAGINATION_API_PORT, SSR_PORT, and SSR_HOST. The SSR example also accepts SSR_HOST to bind a specific host.

```bash
DEMO_PORT=4180 pnpm --dir examples/lit/basic run dev
PAGINATION_DEMO_PORT=4181 PAGINATION_API_PORT=4182 pnpm --dir examples/lit/pagination run dev
SSR_PORT=4180 pnpm --dir examples/lit/ssr run dev
SSR_HOST=0.0.0.0 pnpm --dir examples/lit/ssr run dev
```

const todosOptions = queryOptions({
  queryKey: ['todos'],
  queryFn: fetchTodos,
  initialData: [],
})
```

app.use(VueQueryPlugin)

### getQueryCache() example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryClient.md

Creates a QueryClient, gets its QueryCache, and finds all queries with key ['posts'].

```ts
import { QueryClient } from '@tanstack/query-core'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()
const queries = queryCache.findAll({ queryKey: ['posts'] })
```

--------------------------------

### Set up QueryClientProvider and fetch data with createQuery

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/overview.md

Configure QueryClientProvider at the project root and consume createQuery inside child components. Arguments to createQuery must be wrapped in a function to maintain reactivity in Svelte.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'
  import Example from './lib/Example.svelte'

  const queryClient = new QueryClient()
</script>

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <Example />
</QueryClientProvider>
```

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createQuery } from '@tanstack/svelte-query'

  const query = createQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: () => fetchTodos(),
  }))
</script>

<div>
  {#if query.isPending}
    <p>Loading...</p>
  {:else if query.isError}
    <p>Error: {query.error.message}</p>
  {:else if query.isSuccess}
    {#each query.data as todo}
      <p>{todo.title}</p>
    {/each}
  {/if}
</div>
```

--------------------------------

### Use mutateAsync to get a promise from a mutation

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

Use mutateAsync instead of mutate to get a promise that resolves on success or throws on error. This allows composing side effects with try/catch/finally.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({ mutationFn: addTodo })

try {
  const todo = await mutation.mutateAsync(todo)
  console.log(todo)
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error)
} finally {
  console.log('done')
}
```

### Set up QueryClientProvider with useQuery and useMutation in Preact

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/quick-start.md

Creates a QueryClient and provides it to the app via QueryClientProvider. Uses useQuery to fetch todos and useMutation to add a todo, invalidating the ['todos'] query on success.

```tsx
import {
  useQuery,
  useMutation,
  useQueryClient,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { render } from 'preact'
import { getTodos, postTodo } from '../my-api'

// Create a client
const queryClient = new QueryClient()

function App() {
  return (
    // Provide the client to your App
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Todos />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

function Todos() {
  // Access the client
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  // Queries
  const query = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: getTodos })

  // Mutations
  const mutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: postTodo,
    onSuccess: () => {
      // Invalidate and refetch
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
    },
  })

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {query.data?.map((todo) => (
          <li key={todo.id}>{todo.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <button
        onClick={() => {
          mutation.mutate({
            id: Date.now(),
            title: 'Do Laundry',
          })
        }}
      >
        Add Todo
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

render(<App />, document.getElementById('root'))
```

### useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/functions/useQueryClient.md

Retrieves the QueryClient installed by VueQueryPlugin via Vue's inject. Must be called inside setup() or another function that supports an injection context. Throws if called outside an injection context or if no QueryClient was installed via VueQueryPlugin.

```APIDOC
## useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient

### Description
Retrieves the `QueryClient` installed by `VueQueryPlugin`, via Vue's `inject`. Must be called inside `setup()` or another function that supports an injection context.

### Signature
```ts
function useQueryClient(id?: string): QueryClient;
```

### Parameters
- **id** (`string`, optional, default `''`) - The `queryClientKey` passed to `VueQueryPlugin` — only needed when multiple `QueryClient`s are installed in the same app.

### Returns
- **QueryClient** - The installed `QueryClient`.

### Throws
If called outside an injection context, or if no `QueryClient` was installed via `VueQueryPlugin`.

### Example
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = useQueryClient()

function invalidate() {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
}
</script>
```
```

### setEventListener example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/FocusManager.md

Customizes the focus event listener to use visibilitychange. The setup function registers the listener and returns a cleanup function to remove it when replaced.

```typescript
import { focusManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

focusManager.setEventListener((handleFocus) => {
  const listener = () => handleFocus()
  // Listen to visibilitychange
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.addEventListener) {
    window.addEventListener('visibilitychange', listener, false)
  }

  return () => {
    // Be sure to unsubscribe if a new handler is set
    window.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', listener)
  }
})
```

### Invalidate queries by key prefix

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/guides/query-invalidation.md

Invalidates matching queries starting with the specified queryKey prefix. In this example, both the base 'todos' and the parameterized 'todos' queries are invalidated.

```ts
import { injectQuery, QueryClient } from '@tanstack/angular-query-experimental'

class QueryInvalidationExample {
  readonly queryClient = inject(QueryClient)

  invalidateQueries() {
    this.queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] })
  }

  // Both queries below will be invalidated
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos'],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
  todoListQuery = injectQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['todos', { page: 1 }],
    queryFn: fetchTodoList,
  }))
}
```

### Set custom event listener with setEventListener

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/interfaces/OnlineManager.md

```typescript
import NetInfo from '@react-native-community/netinfo'
import { onlineManager } from '@tanstack/query-core'

onlineManager.setEventListener((setOnline) => {
  return NetInfo.addEventListener((state) => {
    setOnline(!!state.isConnected)
  })
})

### Request Waterfall Example with Article and Comments

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching.md

Shows a request waterfall where Comments query starts only after Article query resolves. Use this to understand the problem before applying prefetching.

```tsx
function Article({ id }) {
  const { data: articleData, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['article', id],
    queryFn: getArticleById,
  })

  if (isPending) {
    return 'Loading article...'
  }

  return (
    <>
      <ArticleHeader articleData={articleData} />
      <ArticleBody articleData={articleData} />
      <Comments id={id} />
    </>
  )
}

function Comments({ id }) {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['article-comments', id],
    queryFn: getArticleCommentsById,
  })

  ...
}
```

### Use mutateAsync with Promise.all for multiple mutations

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/reference/functions/useMutation.md

Callbacks passed to mutate only fire for the last call; use mutateAsync to get a promise per call and await all with Promise.all. This example adds multiple todos and handles errors.

```tsx
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'

function AddTodos() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()

  const addMutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: addTodo,
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] }),
  })

  async function handleAddAll(todos: Array<string>) {
    try {
      await Promise.all(todos.map((todo) => addMutation.mutateAsync(todo)))
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Failed to add todos:', error)
    }
  }

  return (
    <button onClick={() => handleAddAll(['Todo 1', 'Todo 2', 'Todo 3'])}>
      Add all
    </button>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Conditional lazy loading causing double request waterfall

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/prefetching.md

Example from the Performance & Request Waterfalls guide showing a double request waterfall when GraphFeedItem is lazy loaded and its data is fetched only after rendering.

```tsx
// This lazy loads the GraphFeedItem component, meaning
// it won't start loading until something renders it
const GraphFeedItem = React.lazy(() => import('./GraphFeedItem'))

function Feed() {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['feed'],
    queryFn: getFeed,
  })

  if (isPending) {
    return 'Loading feed...'
  }

  return (
    <>
      {data.map((feedItem) => {
        if (feedItem.type === 'GRAPH') {
          return <GraphFeedItem key={feedItem.id} feedItem={feedItem} />
        }

        return <StandardFeedItem key={feedItem.id} feedItem={feedItem} />
      })}
    </>
  )
}

// GraphFeedItem.tsx
function GraphFeedItem({ feedItem }) {
  const { data, isPending } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['graph', feedItem.id],
    queryFn: getGraphDataById,
  })

  ...
}
```

### Augment Register to set defaultError with AxiosError

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/interfaces/Register.md

Augment the installed adapter module's Register interface to override the default error type. This example uses the React adapter; augmenting @tanstack/query-core instead covers every adapter at once.

```ts
// Use the module you installed — here, the React adapter.
declare module '@tanstack/react-query' {
  interface Register {
    defaultError: AxiosError
  }
}
```

### Client entry point: hydrate with HydrationBoundary and QueryClientProvider

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/guides/ssr.md

Creates a client QueryClient and wraps the tree with HydrationBoundary using the dehydrated state read back from the server. Then hydrates the app into the #app element with preactHydrate.

```tsx
import { hydrate as preactHydrate } from 'preact'
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks'
import {
  HydrationBoundary,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/preact-query'

function makeQueryClient() {
  return new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: {
      queries: {
        // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
        // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
        staleTime: 60 * 1000,
      },
    },
  })
}

function App({ dehydratedState }) {
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => makeQueryClient())

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <HydrationBoundary state={dehydratedState}>
        <Posts />
      </HydrationBoundary>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

// Read back and deserialize whatever you embedded on the server,
// e.g. `window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__`
preactHydrate(
  <App dehydratedState={window.__DEHYDRATED_STATE__} />,
  document.getElementById('app'),
)
```

--------------------------------

### Create queryClient inside App with QueryClientProvider for SSR

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/preact/guides/ssr.md

Create the queryClient inside the app using Preact state so each request gets its own cache instead of sharing data between users. The example sets a default staleTime above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client during SSR.

```tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/preact-query'
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks'

// NEVER DO THIS ON THE SERVER:
// const queryClient = new QueryClient()
//
// Creating the queryClient at the module root level makes the cache shared
// between all requests and means _all_ data gets passed to _all_ users.
// Besides being bad for performance, this also leaks any sensitive data.
// (On the client this is fine, since there's only ever one visitor per page.)

export function App({ children }) {
  // Instead do this, which ensures each request has its own cache:
  const [queryClient] = useState(
    () =>
      new QueryClient({
        defaultOptions: {
          queries: {
            // With SSR, we usually want to set some default staleTime
            // above 0 to avoid refetching immediately on the client
            staleTime: 60 * 1000,
          },
        },
      }),
  )

  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

### createInfiniteQueryController

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/lit/reference/functions/createInfiniteQueryController.md

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query. The returned accessor is callable and also exposes current, refetch, fetchNextPage, fetchPreviousPage, and destroy. When options is a function, it is re-read during host updates so query keys and options can follow reactive host state. If queryClient is omitted, the controller resolves the client from the nearest connected QueryClientProvider.

```APIDOC
## createInfiniteQueryController

### Description

Creates a Lit reactive controller that subscribes the host to an infinite query.

### Signature

```ts
function createInfiniteQueryController<
  TQueryFnData = unknown,
  TError = Error,
  TData = InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>,
  TQueryKey extends readonly unknown[] = readonly unknown[],
  TPageParam = unknown
>(
  host: ReactiveControllerHost,
  options: Accessor<
    CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>
  >,
  queryClient?: QueryClient
): InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>;
```

### Type Parameters

- **TQueryFnData** = `unknown`
- **TError** = `Error`
- **TData** = `InfiniteData<TQueryFnData, unknown>`
- **TQueryKey** extends `readonly unknown[]` = `readonly unknown[]`
- **TPageParam** = `unknown`

### Parameters

- **host** (`ReactiveControllerHost`) - The Lit reactive controller host that owns the infinite query subscription.
- **options** (`Accessor<CreateInfiniteQueryOptions<TQueryFnData, TError, TData, TQueryKey, TPageParam>>`) - Infinite query observer options, or a getter that returns options.
- **queryClient?** (`QueryClient`) - Optional explicit query client. Provide this for controllers that should not resolve a client from Lit context.

### Returns

`InfiniteQueryResultAccessor<TData, TError>` - An accessor for the latest infinite query result with page helper methods.

### Example

```ts
import { LitElement, html } from 'lit'
import { createInfiniteQueryController } from '@tanstack/lit-query'

class ProjectsView extends LitElement {
  private readonly projects = createInfiniteQueryController(this, {
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) => fetchProjects(pageParam),
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.nextCursor,
  })

  render() {
    const query = this.projects()

    return html`
      <button ?disabled=${!query.hasNextPage} @click=${() => this.projects.fetchNextPage()}>
        Load more
      </button>
    `
  }
}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Configure useMutation with a scope id to serialize mutations

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations.md

By default all mutations run in parallel, even repeated calls to the same mutation. Giving mutations the same scope.id runs them in serial: a triggered mutation starts in isPaused: true if another mutation for that scope is in progress, is queued, and resumes automatically when its turn comes.

```tsx
const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: addTodo,
  scope: {
    id: 'todo',
  },
})
```

### Create withSetup helper for Vue 2 using createLocalVue

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/guides/testing.md

Uses `createLocalVue` and `localVue.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })` to install the plugin. With Vue 2.6, also call `localVue.use(VueCompositionApi)` before installing `VueQueryPlugin` and import `VueCompositionApi` and `defineComponent` from `@vue/composition-api`.

```ts
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import { createLocalVue, mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import flushPromises from 'flush-promises'
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

function withSetup<T>(composable: () => T, queryClient = new QueryClient()) {
  let result!: T
  const localVue = createLocalVue()
  localVue.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })
  const wrapper = mount(
    defineComponent({
      setup() {
        result = composable()
        return () => null
      },
    }),
    { localVue },
  )
  return [result, wrapper] as const
}
```

### Pass options as a function to useQuery in Solid Query

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md

Solid Query primitives like useQuery, useMutation, and useIsFetching take arguments as functions so they can be tracked in a reactive scope. The React-style object argument is shown as incorrect.

```tsx
// ❌ react version
useQuery({
  queryKey: ['todos', todo],
  queryFn: fetchTodos,
})

// ✅ solid version
useQuery(() => ({
  queryKey: ['todos', todo],
  queryFn: fetchTodos,
}))
```

### VueQueryPlugin.install

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/vue/reference/variables/VueQueryPlugin.md

Installs a QueryClient on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through useQueryClient. Accepts the Vue app instance and optional VueQueryPluginOptions (defaulting to an empty object). Returns void.

```APIDOC
## VueQueryPlugin.install

### Description
Installs a `QueryClient` on the Vue app, making it available to every descendant component through `useQueryClient` — the Vue equivalent of React's `QueryClientProvider`, but wired up as an app-level plugin instead of a wrapping component.

### Method
`install`

### Signature
```ts
install: (app: any, options: VueQueryPluginOptions) => void;
```

### Parameters
- **app** (`any`) - The Vue app instance.
- **options** (`VueQueryPluginOptions`) - Optional. Defaults to `{}`.

### Returns
`void`

### Example
```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const app = createApp(App)
app.use(VueQueryPlugin)
```

Pass a `queryClient` you constructed yourself — useful for SSR, where you need a fresh `QueryClient` per request, or when the same instance also needs to be used outside of Vue components:
```ts
import { QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin } from '@tanstack/vue-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, { queryClient })
```

Or pass `queryClientConfig` to let the plugin construct the `QueryClient` for you, with your own defaults:
```ts
app.use(VueQueryPlugin, {
  queryClientConfig: {
    defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 5 * 1000 } },
  },
})
```
```

### Basic useQuery example fetching GitHub repo data

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/overview.md

A minimal React component that uses QueryClientProvider and useQuery to fetch and display TanStack Query's GitHub repository stats. It handles loading and error states.

```tsx
import {
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
  useQuery,
} from '@tanstack/react-query'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

export default function App() {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Example />
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}

function Example() {
  const { isPending, error, data } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['repoData'],
    queryFn: async () => {
      const response = await fetch(
        'https://api.github.com/repos/TanStack/query',
      )
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch repo data')
      return response.json()
    },
  })

  if (isPending) return 'Loading...'

  if (error) return 'An error has occurred: ' + error.message

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>{data.name}</h1>
      <p>{data.description}</p>
      <strong>👀 {data.subscribers_count}</strong>{' '}
      <strong>✨ {data.stargazers_count}</strong>{' '}
      <strong>🍴 {data.forks_count}</strong>
    </div>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### Implement basic infinite scrolling with useInfiniteQuery in Solid

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/solid/guides/infinite-queries.md

Fetches paginated project data using useInfiniteQuery and renders pages with SolidJS control flow components, including loading state, error state, and a load more button.

```tsx
import { Switch, Match, For, Show } from 'solid-js'
import { useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/solid-query'

function Projects() {
  const fetchProjects = async ({ pageParam }) => {
    const res = await fetch('/api/projects?cursor=' + pageParam)
    return res.json()
  }

  const projectsQuery = useInfiniteQuery(() => ({
    queryKey: ['projects'],
    queryFn: fetchProjects,
    initialPageParam: 0,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage, pages) => lastPage.nextCursor,
  }))

  return (
    <Switch>
      <Match when={projectsQuery.isPending}>
        <p>Loading...</p>
      </Match>
      <Match when={projectsQuery.isError}>
        <p>Error: {projectsQuery.error.message}</p>
      </Match>
      <Match when={projectsQuery.isSuccess}>
        <For each={projectsQuery.data.pages}>
          {(group) => (
            <For each={group.data}>{(project) => <p>{project.name}</p>}</For>
          )}
        </For>
        <div>
          <button
            onClick={() => projectsQuery.fetchNextPage()}
            disabled={!projectsQuery.hasNextPage || projectsQuery.isFetching}
          >
            {projectsQuery.isFetchingNextPage
              ? 'Loading more...'
              : projectsQuery.hasNextPage
                ? 'Load More'
                : 'Nothing more to load'}
          </button>
        </div>
        <Show
          when={projectsQuery.isFetching && !projectsQuery.isFetchingNextPage}
        >
          <div>Fetching...</div>
        </Show>
      </Match>
    </Switch>
  )
}
```

--------------------------------

### restoreQueries(queryClient: QueryClient, filters): Promise<void>

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/react/plugins/createPersister.md

Restores queries that are currently stored by the persister, for example when the app starts in offline mode or to make previous session data immediately available without a loading state. The filter object supports queryKey and exact properties. The storage must expose an entries method that returns a key-value tuple array.

```APIDOC
## restoreQueries(queryClient: QueryClient, filters): Promise<void>

### Description
This function can be used to restore queries that are currently stored by persister. For example when your app is starting up in offline mode, or you want all or only specific data from previous session to be immediately available without intermediate `loading` state.

For this function to work, your storage must expose `entries` method that would return a `key-value tuple array`. For example `Object.entries(localStorage)` for `localStorage` or `entries` from `idb-keyval`.

### Method
restoreQueries

### Parameters
- **queryClient** (QueryClient) - Required - The QueryClient instance.
- **filters** (object) - Required - Filter object with the following properties:
  - **queryKey** (QueryKey) - Optional - Set this property to define a query key to match on.
  - **exact** (boolean) - Optional - If you don't want to search queries inclusively by query key, you can pass the `exact: true` option to return only the query with the exact query key you have passed.

### Response
Returns a Promise<void>.
```

### clear method example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/svelte/reference/classes/QueryCache.md

Example usage of the clear method to remove all queries from the cache.

```ts
const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()

queryCache.clear()
```

--------------------------------

### findAll() Example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/QueryCache.md

Retrieves all queries from the cache that partially match the given query key. Returns an empty array if no queries match.

```ts
const queryCache = queryClient.getQueryCache()

const queries = queryCache.findAll({ queryKey: ['posts'] })
```

### setOptions method example

Source: https://github.com/tanstack/query/blob/main/docs/framework/angular/reference/classes/MutationObserver.md

Sets new options including a mutationFn and onSuccess callback. The options are defaulted with QueryClient#defaultMutationOptions before being applied.

```ts
observer.setOptions({
  mutationFn: (variables: { title: string }) => addPost(variables),
  onSuccess: (data) => console.log(data),
})
```
